newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Food shares halt Nigerian market slump.
newsitem.headline: Food shares halt Nigerian market slump.

text.p: Robust gains by food shares led by a surging Nestle put a brake on Nigeria's falling stock market, which ended slightly higher on Thursday.
The all share index closed at 8566.78 from 8564.27, its first rise in recent weeks, dealers said.
They said gains in food shares combined with a lull in price drops on Thursday was mainly responsible for the rise of the index.
But one said: "It is too early yet to expect the end of recent bearish trend."
Traders said stock prices had been falling because of the outflow of funds to money markets, among other reasons.
Nestle closed 75 kobo up at 45.55 naira as investor interest in its shares continued to rise.
Flour Mills also kept up its strong posture in anticipation of a good year-end result. It ended at 16.85 naira, up 10 kobo.
Conglomerates saw little activity with UTC rising two kobo to 1.36 naira. Sectoral leaders PZ Industries Lever Brothers and UAC were all unchanged.
The petroleum sector was largely unchanged except for a 20 kobo slide in Agip stock to 20.80 naira.
Wema Bank closed five kobo up at 2.95 naira while Afribank finished five kobo down at 7.70 naira.
